[i2t]lte_ocean_currency=Nutrients[i2t]lte_ocean_logline=Explore the vast, dark, deep ocean and the extremely weird animals that manage to call this hostile environment home.[i2t]lte_ocean_g_sunlight_zone=Sunlight Zone[i2t]lte_ocean_g_sunlight_zone_desc=Sunlight defines the epipelagic zone, the top layer of open ocean. [i2t]lte_ocean_r_detritus=Sinking Detritus[i2t]lte_ocean_r_detritus_desc=After eating phytoplankton or each other, animals excrete waste full of carbon, nitrogen, and other nutrients. [i2t]lte_ocean_r_making_light=Making Light[i2t]lte_ocean_r_making_light_desc=Life that can glow is rare on land, but it’s the rule in the dark sea. Up to 90% of deep dwellers are bioluminescent. [i2t]lte_ocean_r_seeing_blue=Seeing Blue[i2t]lte_ocean_r_seeing_blue_desc=Twilight eyes are tuned to blue light. The planet's surface absorbs solar energy and reflects the heat into the atmosphere, creating weather, water cycles, and climate.[i2t]lte_atmos_g_troposphere=Troposphere[i2t]lte_atmos_g_troposphere_desc=The atmosphere extends upward from the Earth's surface. The troposphere is about 13km tall and contains most of the planet's life. As warm air rises and cold air sinks, this layer experiences turbulence and weather.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_air=Air[i2t]lte_atmos_r_air_desc=Invisible and odorless, air is a mixture of gases held in place by gravity. Important components of troposphere air are oxygen, which humans and animals breathe, and carbon dioxide, which is metabolized by plants.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_nitrogen=Nitrogen[i2t]lte_atmos_r_nitrogen_desc=The most abundant element in Earth's lower atmosphere, nitrogen (N2) makes up 78% of the troposphere. When exposed to specialized microbes or lightning, nitrogen is converted into compounds that form amino acids and DNA.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_oxygen=Oxygen[i2t]lte_atmos_r_oxygen_desc=When two oxygen (O) atoms bond, molecular oxygen (O2) is produced. A relative latecomer to the Earth's atmosphere, oxygen is introduced billions of years ago, when photosynthesizing bacteria enter the ecosystem.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_water=Water[i2t]lte_atmos_r_water_desc=Two hydrogen atoms bonded with a single oxygen atom create a highly stable molecule, water. On Earth, water moves through a continuous cycle of evaporation, condensation, and precipitation, and can be a solid, liquid, or gas.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_sunlight=Sunlight[i2t]lte_atmos_r_sunlight_desc=The Sun emits many forms of energy, including electromagnetic waves, which do not require a medium to move. A combination of these waves travels through the vacuum of space, taking approximately 8 minutes to reach Earth as sunlight.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_infrared_radiation=Infrared Radiation[i2t]lte_atmos_r_infrared_radiation_desc=The majority of the Sun's energy is infrared, a type of electromagnetic radiation. Invisible to the human eye, this energy is constantly absorbed by objects exposed to the sun and emitted as heat.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_vapor=Vapor[i2t]lte_atmos_r_vapor_desc=Liquid substances can become temporarily gaseous through evaporation or boiling. Exposure to cooling or pressure converts it back. Liquid water evaporates into vapor when exposed to the sun's heat.[i2t]lte_atmos_g_clouds=Cloud[i2t]lte_atmos_g_clouds_desc=As warm, moist air rises, it expands while air pressure decreases, causing the vapor to cool. Its molecules attach to airborne particles, condensing into liquid droplets and ice crystals, forming a cloud.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_cumulus=Cumulus[i2t]lte_atmos_r_cumulus_desc=The classic fair-weather cloud, a cumulus is white, puffy, and cotton-like. While it usually indicates sunny weather, in turbulent conditions, it can swell into a storm cloud.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_cirrus=Cirrus[i2t]lte_atmos_r_cirrus_desc=Wispy and feathery clouds are formed when warm, dry air rises to high altitudes, and water vapor attaches to dust and turns to ice. An increase in cirrus clouds can signal an approaching storm system.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_stratus=Stratus[i2t]lte_atmos_r_stratus_desc=A common, low-lying cloud, stratus clouds are layered and opaque, covering much of the sky. They can appear as a blanket of gentle stripes or a wall of darkness.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_pressure=Pressure[i2t]lte_atmos_r_pressure_desc=The atmosphere has mass. Each air molecule is pulled downwards by gravity, giving the air weight, known as pressure. High pressure suggests clear weather, while low pressure indicates turbulence.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_wild=Wind[i2t]lte_atmos_r_wild_desc=While the Earth's surface continuously reflects the Sun's heat into the air, it does so unevenly. As warm air rises, cooler air quickly sinks into the vacated space, producing kinetic energy in the form of wind.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_fronts=Fronts[i2t]lte_atmos_r_fronts_desc=When two contrasting air masses meet, weather is destabilized, creating a front. Warm fronts cause a gentle transition of weather, while cold fronts are violent, bringing severe weather like thunderstorms and gusty winds.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_jet_stream=Jet Stream[i2t]lte_atmos_r_jet_stream_desc=The sun heats the equator more than the Earth's poles, forming contrasting fields of temperature and air density. When they meet, they create jet streams: fast-flowing currents in the upper troposphere that flow west to east.[i2t]lte_atmos_g_storm=Storm[i2t]lte_atmos_g_storm_desc=When warm, moist air rises and condenses into towering cumulonimbus clouds, it releases substantial amounts of heat energy. This can create heavy winds, torrential rains, lightning, hail, or even tornadoes.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_cumulunimbus=Cumulonimbus[i2t]lte_atmos_r_cumulunimbus_desc=When fair-weather cumulus clouds grow vertically, they can form into cumulonimbus clouds. These dense, towering, anvil-shaped clouds can be as big as 10 km in height, and bring thunderstorms, hail, and severe weather conditions.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_rain=Precipitation[i2t]lte_atmos_r_rain_desc=When the water droplets that form clouds grow in size and weight, they are eventually pulled back down by gravity. Depending on the temperature, they can take the form of rain, sleet, snow, or hail.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_tornado=Tornado[i2t]lte_atmos_r_tornado_desc=Violent, opposing winds can pull at clouds in a thunderstorm, forming a spinning column of air, water, and debris that extends to the ground. With winds over 200 mph, these funnel-shaped clouds can cause extreme destruction.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_lightning=Lightning[i2t]lte_atmos_r_lightning_desc=Colliding particles build up static electricity within a storm, bursting from the cloud as a sudden electrostatic discharge. It superheats the air and glows brightly, traveling between clouds or striking the ground.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_thunder=Thunder[i2t]lte_atmos_r_thunder_desc=When lightning superheats the air, explosive heat forces it to expand, then contract as it cools. This creates an audible shockwave called a thunderclap. The sound is heard after a lightning strike, as light travels faster than sound.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_nimbostratus=Nimbostratus[i2t]lte_atmos_r_nimbostratus_desc=Forming a dark, thick layer that blocks out the sun, a nimbostratus cloud causes continuous rain or snow, but no lightning or thunder. It forms in the middle troposphere, then spreads to lower and higher levels.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_mammatus=Mammatus[i2t]lte_atmos_r_mammatus_desc=Unlike most clouds, a mammatus forms when heavy, cold air sinks into warmer air beneath. The bubble-like cloud formations sag beneath a parent cloud, usually a cumulonimbus. Pilots avoid flying through these turbulent clouds.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_lenticular=Lenticular[i2t]lte_atmos_r_lenticular_desc=When air travels over a barrier like a mountain or building, it is forced up, causing it to expand, cool, then condense. The resulting saucer-shaped cloud is stationary even in turbulent conditions, appearing to hover in the sky.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_asperitas=Asperitas[i2t]lte_atmos_r_asperitas_desc=A supplementary attribute of certain clouds, the asperitas is a rare formation with an underside that resembles upside-down ocean waves. They are widespread in the plains of the United States and often appear after thunderstorms.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_visible_light=Visible Light[i2t]lte_atmos_r_visible_light_desc=There is only a small portion of the electromagnetic spectrum that the human eye can detect. Cone cells allow the brain to interpret wavelengths as specific colors. White light is a combination of all colors on the spectrum.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_rainbow=Rainbow[i2t]lte_atmos_r_rainbow_desc=When light is reflected, refracted, and dispersed through droplets in the atmosphere, it creates an optical illusion called a rainbow. It separates light into a sequence of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_uv_radiation=UV Radiation[i2t]lte_atmos_r_uv_radiation_desc=Making up a small percentage of sunlight, ultraviolet radiation sits on the spectrum between visible light and X-rays. Humans need UV to produce vitamin D, but overexposure causes sunburns, damages DNA, and leads to cancer.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_ozone=Ozone[i2t]lte_atmos_r_ozone_desc=UV light splits diatomic oxygen (O2) into separate oxygen atoms (O) which re-bond to form ozone (O3), a blue gas with a pungent odor. In the stratosphere, ozone molecules form a shield that protects life below from UV rays.[i2t]lte_atmos_g_stratosphere=Stratosphere[i2t]lte_atmos_g_stratosphere_desc=Above the troposphere lies the stratosphere, a layer where heated ozone causes temperatures to increase with altitude. This creates more stable conditions than below, making it an ideal altitude for planes to fly.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_ozone_layer=Ozone Layer[i2t]lte_atmos_r_ozone_layer_desc=Reacting to high levels of UV rays, ozone molecules are continuously being created and destroyed. High concentrations of ozone in the stratosphere absorb harmful radiation that could cause mass extinction on the surface.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_blue_jet=Blue Jet Lightning[i2t]lte_atmos_r_blue_jet_desc=A rare form of bright blue, upward-shooting lightning can erupt from the top of cumulonimbus clouds. Blue jet lightning gets its color from nitrogen gas as it travels into the stratosphere.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_polar_vortex=Polar Vortex[i2t]lte_atmos_r_polar_vortex_desc=High in the stratosphere, massive, counterclockwise spinning weather systems lock in icy air over the Arctic. They destabilize in winter and spill southward, causing sudden temperature drops in mid-latitude regions like the US.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_nacreous_clouds=Nacreous Clouds[i2t]lte_atmos_r_nacreous_clouds_desc=Found near the Earth's poles, nacreous clouds only form high up in the stratosphere. Their tiny ice crystals bend and separate sunlight into pastel colors. They contain nitrous oxide (N2O), which damages the ozone layer.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_blue_sky=Blue Sky[i2t]lte_atmos_r_blue_sky_desc=As sunlight reaches the Earth's atmosphere, it hits air molecules, scattering the white light into its spectrum. Due to its shorter wavelengths, blue light gets scattered more, making the sky appear blue during the day.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_black_sky=Black Sky[i2t]lte_atmos_r_black_sky_desc=When ascending through the atmosphere, the air becomes thinner, with fewer air molecules to scatter sunlight. This causes the sky to gradually darken from blue to black. Without an atmosphere, the sky would be black at both day and night.[i2t]lte_atmos_g_mesosphere=Mesosphere[i2t]lte_atmos_g_mesosphere_desc=Too high for balloons yet too low to be studied with satellites, the mesosphere is the least understood layer. With temperatures as low as -143°C, it is the coldest part of the atmosphere, as thin air absorbs little sunlight.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_meteor=Meteoric Smoke Particles[i2t]lte_atmos_r_meteor_desc=Each day, 48.5 tons of meteoric material burn up in Earth's atmosphere, leaving behind a haze of fine metallic particulates. As it seeps down into the lower atmosphere, meteor smoke influences tropospheric cloud formation.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_shooting_stars=Shooting Stars[i2t]lte_atmos_r_shooting_stars_desc=The vast majority of atmospheric meteors are no more than a few millimeters in size. Travelling at hypersonic speeds, most burn up entirely, briefly shining bright like a star.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_sprites=Sprites[i2t]lte_atmos_r_sprites_desc=Appearing at altitudes of 65-75 km, sprites can form when a cloud's electrical charge is released upwards rather than downwards. Red in color, sprites last for about a millisecond and can extend as wide as 48 km in diameter.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_noctilucent=Noctilucent Clouds[i2t]lte_atmos_r_noctilucent_desc=Usually observed near sunrise and sunset, noctilucent clouds reflect sunlight from below the horizon. The highest clouds in Earth's atmosphere, they often form around the remnants of burned-up micrometeors.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_elves=ELVES[i2t]lte_atmos_r_elves_desc=Lightning strikes generate electromagnetic pulses, which can interact with nitrogen molecules in the air, creating ELVES. These rapidly expanding red rings over storm clouds last for under a millisecond and can span 400 km across.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_turbopause=Turbopause[i2t]lte_atmos_r_turbopause_desc=The boundary between the mesosphere and thermosphere, the turbopause averages at -90℃. It marks the point where gases are no longer mixed by winds and weather but are instead separated by molecular weight.[i2t]lte_atmos_g_thermosphere=Thermosphere[i2t]lte_atmos_g_thermosphere_desc=Solar radiation makes the thermosphere the hottest layer of the atmosphere, heated to temperatures as high as 2,000°C. However, the air is so thin that molecules cannot transfer their heat, so to a human it would feel cold.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_karman_line=Karman Line[i2t]lte_atmos_r_karman_line_desc=Located 100km above Earth, the Karman Line is the internationally recognized border between the atmosphere and outer space. At this point the atmosphere becomes so thin that an object needs to reach orbital velocity to stay aloft.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_ionized_gas=Plasma[i2t]lte_atmos_r_ionized_gas_desc=Supercharged by radiation, atoms are stripped of electrons, creating a fourth state of matter called plasma. This mix of free-floating electrons and positive ions conducts electricity and reacts to magnetic and electric fields.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_electron=Electron[i2t]lte_atmos_r_electron_desc=A subatomic particle with a negative electric charge can exist freely, or bound to the nucleus of an atom, where it becomes a building block of matter. The earliest electrons formed during the first microsecond of the Big Bang.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_positive_ion=Positive Ion[i2t]lte_atmos_r_positive_ion_desc=An atom or molecule that loses one or more electrons is left with a positive charge. In the thermosphere, electrons are torn from gas particles by solar photons, creating electrically-charged positive ions.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_proton=Airglow[i2t]lte_atmos_r_proton_desc=The Earth's night sky is never fully dark. Airglow is a faint, ever-present swirl of light in the upper atmosphere that envelops the planet. It is the result of plasma cooling back into a neutral state and releasing light energy.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_cosmic_rays=Cosmic Rays[i2t]lte_atmos_r_cosmic_rays_desc=Originating from the Sun and massive cosmic events such as black holes and supernovas, long-range ionizing rays constantly hit the Earth. While most are deflected, they can trigger lightning and affect electronics on the ground.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_plasma_bubbles=Plasma Bubbles[i2t]lte_atmos_r_plasma_bubbles_desc=During the day, ionized plasma travels along Earth's magnetic field. At night, these bands of plasma disappear, leaving behind bubbles of low-density gas in the atmosphere that can disrupt radio waves and GPS.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_solar_winds=Solar Wind[i2t]lte_atmos_r_solar_winds_desc=The Sun blasts out a stream of charged electrons and protons at a million miles per hour, forming the heliosphere. In Earth's magnetic field, these particles collide with atmospheric gases, producing northern and southern lights.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_aurora_borealis=Aurora[i2t]lte_atmos_r_aurora_borealis_desc=Charged particles are funneled toward Earth's magnetic poles, ionizing atoms in the thermosphere to create spectacular light shows visible from the surface. The most famous is the Aurora Borealis, also known as Northern Lights.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_magnetosphere=Magnetosphere[i2t]lte_atmos_r_magnetosphere_desc=The Earth's core generates a magnetic field that extends thousands of kilometers into space. It deflects solar winds, solar flares, and cosmic rays, acting as the first line of defense for every layer of the atmosphere below.[i2t]lte_atmos_r_ionosphere=Ionosphere[i2t]lte_atmos_r_ionosphere_desc=The thermosphere is home to a region of plasma called the ionosphere. It fluctuates daily: highly active during the day, it relaxes into a thinner layer at night as particles return to more neutral states.[i2t]lte_atmos_g_exosphere=Exosphere[i2t]lte_atmos_g_exosphere_desc=The outermost layer of Earth's atmosphere begins 500km above sea level and reaches halfway to the Moon. As you go up, the air thins into the vacuum of space and offers a nearly frictionless orbital zone for satellites.[i2t]lte_atmos_outro_1=The atmosphere is a system that supports and shapes the life within it.[i2t]lte_atmos_outro_2=It is ruled by forces interacting to create a unique and delicate balance.[i2t]lte_atmos_outro_3=From beneath its protective layers, life can safely marvel at the vast brutality of space.

The mother's body protects the growing fetus, keeps it warm, and supplies it with the nutrients it needs to develop.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_reproductive=Reproductive System[i2t]lte_fetus_r_reproductive_desc=The female reproductive system is made up of two ovaries and fallopian tubes connected to the uterus. The ovaries house millions of reproductive cells, called eggs. A female is born with all of the eggs they will ever have.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_egg=Egg[i2t]lte_fetus_r_egg_desc=Containing nutrients for early development and 23 chromosomes, an egg is released into a fallopian tube every month or so. The uterine lining thickens, but if the egg is not fertilized, the lining sheds during a menstrual period.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_sperm=Sperm[i2t]lte_fetus_r_sperm_desc=The male reproductive cell is made of three parts. The head contains the enzymes required to penetrate an egg, along with 23 chromosomes. The middle houses energy for movement, and its whip-like tail propels it forward.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_fertilization=Fertilization[i2t]lte_fetus_r_fertilization_desc=Around 300 million sperm are released during sex, travelling through the uterus into the fallopian tube. Chemicals released by the egg influence and guide certain sperm, allowing only one to fertilize it and begin a pregnancy.[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_1=Month One[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_1_desc=The first month of pregnancy is a period of preparation: the body releases hormones like estrogen and progesterone, causing the lining of the uterus to thicken. This creates a foundation for a fertilized egg to implant and grow.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_zygote=Zygote[i2t]lte_fetus_r_zygote_desc=A fertilized egg, called a zygote, is a single cell containing a combined 46 chromosomes from the egg and sperm. It travels back down the fallopian tubes, dividing into more and more cells on the way to the uterus.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_multiples=Multiples[i2t]lte_fetus_r_multiples_desc=The possibility of a multiple pregnancy occurs at fertilization. When one egg splits, it creates identical siblings with the same genetic information. Fraternal siblings result from several eggs fertilized by different sperm.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_eat_drink=Diet Limits[i2t]lte_fetus_r_eat_drink_desc=The fetus is fragile, and any stressors are dangerous for its development. Raw foods can contain harmful bacteria, and alcohol absorbs directly into the bloodstream, all of which can lead to permanent damage after birth.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_blastocyst=Blastocyst[i2t]lte_fetus_r_blastocyst_desc=Over the next week, the zygote's cells rapidly divide and multiply, forming a ball of hundreds of cells. Now called a blastocyst, its outer layer burrows into the uterus, implanting itself and forming the placenta.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_embryo=Embryo[i2t]lte_fetus_r_embryo_desc=After the outer layer of the blastocyst implants into the uterine lining, the bundle of cells, now called an embryo, starts to grow. This stage of development and differentiation lasts for about 8 weeks.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_placenta=Placenta[i2t]lte_fetus_r_placenta_desc=A temporary, shared organ between mother and child called the placenta develops alongside the embryo. Before the fetus's own organs form, the placenta acts as its external lung, kidney, and endocrine gland.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_amniotic_sac=Amniotic Sac[i2t]lte_fetus_r_amniotic_sac_desc=Formed from cells of the blastocyst, the amniotic sac is a pair of membranes surrounding the embryo. Within it is amniotic fluid, a water-based liquid that cushions the embryo, regulates body temperature, and provides nutrients.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_missed_period=Confirmation[i2t]lte_fetus_r_missed_period_desc=A missed period is usually the first sign of a possible pregnancy, as successful implantation halts the menstrual period. An at-home pregnancy test can be used to detect hCG in urine, a hormone created after implantation.[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_2=Month Two[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_2_desc=The embryo is only the size of a sesame seed, but it is already growing foundational structures that will later become organs. Meanwhile, the mother's heart beats harder and faster than before to produce more blood.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_neural_tube=Neural Tube[i2t]lte_fetus_r_neural_tube_desc=A hollow structure along the embryo's back is actually the proto-version of the embryo's nervous system. Over time, this tube expands in two opposing directions and eventually develops into the spinal cord and the brain.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_heart_tube=Heart Tube[i2t]lte_fetus_r_heart_tube_desc=The first functional organ to develop is the heart, which starts as a tube of cells. By week 6, it is already pulsing at an average of 110 beats per minute. Eventually, it twists around itself to form a four-chambered structure.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_body_form=The Body Forms[i2t]lte_fetus_r_body_form_desc=By week 6, the embryo's body takes shape: internal organs differentiate themselves, small buds appear that will become limbs, and blood starts circulating. By week 7, bones form, limbs grow, and brain development accelerates.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_umbilical=Umbilical Cord[i2t]lte_fetus_r_umbilical_desc=The tube that connects a developing fetus to the mother's placenta is fully operational by week 7. Through the umbilical cord, the mother supplies the fetus with oxygen and nutrients, and filters waste back to the mother's body.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_morning_sickness=Morning Sickness[i2t]lte_fetus_r_morning_sickness_desc=Affecting up to 70% of all mothers, nausea and vomiting are experienced during pregnancy. Despite the name, morning sickness can happen at any time of day. This queasiness is likely caused by hormones produced by the placenta.[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_3=Month Three[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_3_desc=The embryo is the size of a plum by the third month of pregnancy. This is the time when parents-to-be can see the fetal heartbeat for the first time on an ultrasound, and typically announce their pregnancy to others.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_fetus=Fetus[i2t]lte_fetus_r_fetus_desc=An embryo becomes a fetus after all of its major organs have formed. The fetus is approximately half an inch long, and its growth shifts gears from development to maturation.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_amniotic_fluid=Amniotic Fluid[i2t]lte_fetus_r_amniotic_fluid_desc=The fetus is suspended in a clear liquid that is mostly water from the mother's body. Over the course of the pregnancy, the fetus breathes it in, swallows it, and urinates it out, until the fluid mostly consists of yellow urine.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_cravings=Cravings[i2t]lte_fetus_r_cravings_desc=A sudden, intense urge to eat specific foods might start in the first trimester. This craving for foods that the mother might normally dislike is often driven by changing hormones and new nutritional needs due to the pregnancy.[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_4=Month Four[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_4_desc=At the beginning of the second trimester, morning sickness may subside, but cravings can intensify. The now avocado-sized fetus continues to grow, requires more nutrients, and pushes against the mother's digestive system.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_genitals=Reproductive Organs[i2t]lte_fetus_r_genitals_desc=A fetus's chromosomal sex is set at fertilization, but there are no visible differences between sexes in the first weeks. External genitals differentiate during the second trimester, driven primarily by genetic signals and hormones.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_organ_move=Organ Function[i2t]lte_fetus_r_organ_move_desc=No longer fully dependent on the mother, the fetus's organs are now beginning to function. The liver and spleen produce the first red blood cells, the intestines move to their permanent location, and thin, translucent skin forms.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_reactions=Rudimentary Senses[i2t]lte_fetus_r_reactions_desc=By the second trimester, the brain has billions of neurons, and the fetus shows reflexes like swallowing and movement. It cannot clearly hear the outside world, but it can sense internal sounds like the mother's heartbeat.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_milk_glands=Milk Glands[i2t]lte_fetus_r_milk_glands_desc=Lactogenesis begins around week 16, as estrogen and progesterone create an increase in milk ducts as the breasts prepare to produce milk for a newborn. The mother's breasts grow, the nipples darken, and the areolas become larger.[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_5=Month Five[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_5_desc=By the halfway point of the pregnancy, the fetus is the size of a mango and weighs about a pound. The mother's body is holding more fluid, which often gathers in the lowest parts of the body and causes swelling in the feet.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_skin=Fetal Skin[i2t]lte_fetus_r_skin_desc=The fetus's translucent skin thickens and develops a temporary outer layer, called vernix, to protect against amniotic fluid. Fine hairs called lanugo also grow, keeping the fetus warm and also protecting the skin.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_kicks=Kicks and Punches[i2t]lte_fetus_r_kicks_desc=The fetus makes its first noticeable movements by the fifth month, which can feel like butterflies in the mother's stomach. As the fetus grows larger and has less room, a mother may feel its kicks and punches more often.[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_6=Month Six[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_6_desc=Veins are visible through the fetus' translucent skin, making it appear red in color. Eyebrows, eyelashes, fingernails, and toenails have formed. It can even scratch itself, but its nails are not sharp enough to cause any harm.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_bone_marrow=Bone Marrow[i2t]lte_fetus_r_bone_marrow_desc=Blood-forming stem cells travel from the fetus's liver and spleen to newly formed bone marrow as the skeletal system matures. By the end of month six, this new marrow takes over as the dominant blood producer.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_hearing=Hearing[i2t]lte_fetus_r_hearing_desc=With the ears more developed, the fetus can now hear muffled sounds like music from outside the womb. It is already beginning to process language and can even differentiate its mother from unfamiliar voices[i2t]lte_fetus_r_lungs=Lungs[i2t]lte_fetus_r_lungs_desc=The fetus practices breathing by inhaling and exhaling amniotic fluid, receiving oxygen through the umbilical cord. Later, the fetus produces surfactant, a liquid that lines the alveoli to prevent their collapse.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_week_23=Pre-Term Birth[i2t]lte_fetus_r_week_23_desc=If a baby is born alive before the end of the pregnancy, it is considered pre-term. Early arrival means the fetus misses vital time for organs like the lungs and brain to fully mature, and might require intensive care to survive.[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_7=Month Seven[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_7_desc=Amniotic fluid begins to reduce, and the fetus gains more body fat. The fetus is now 2 pounds, about the size of a large eggplant. This compresses the mother's organs, making it harder to breathe and causing her to pee more often.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_melanin=Opaque Skin[i2t]lte_fetus_r_melanin_desc=The fetus's translucent skin becomes opaque as the skin thickens and accumulates fat. Melanin production accelerates around this time, setting skin tone and protecting the fetus from the sun once it leaves the womb.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_blinking=Blinking[i2t]lte_fetus_r_blinking_desc=The eyes remain sealed for protection until around week 26, when they open for the first time. The fetus blinks to build eye muscle strength, test the nervous system, and respond to changes in light.[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_8=Month Eight[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_8_desc=The third trimester marks the last phase of the pregnancy before birth. The fetus is now 5 pounds and the size of a honeydew melon. It spends most of its time sleeping, but perks up when the mother eats or drinks something sugary.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_brain=Brain[i2t]lte_fetus_r_brain_desc=Neural development accelerates in the final months of pregnancy. The brain triples in size, growing up to 11 ounces in weight. Grooves and ridges form in the cerebrum, and 40,000 new connections are made every second.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_body_heat=Independence[i2t]lte_fetus_r_body_heat_desc=While still dependent, the fetus starts to rely less on its mother. As its muscles and nervous system mature, it takes on more of its own functions, such as practicing movement, breathing consistently, and even smiling.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_braxton=False Labor[i2t]lte_fetus_r_braxton_desc=In the later months of pregnancy, the mother may experience sporadic uterine-tightening contractions. Less intense and consistent than actual labor, these 'practice contractions' are thought to prepare the body for true labor.[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_9=Month Nine[i2t]lte_fetus_g_month_9_desc=Fetal growth is in its final stage. The fetus rapidly gains fat to help regulate body temperature and blood sugar. It should also turn to face downward in preparation for birth. The mother is looking forward to a successful birth.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_thirst=Fluid Balance[i2t]lte_fetus_r_thirst_desc=The fetus now drinks a pint of amniotic fluid a day to practice swallowing and urinating. The plate is separated by flexible joints, helping the fetus safely exit the narrow birth canal. By the baby's second birthday, the skull is mostly hardened.[i2t]lte_fetus_r_hair=Hair[i2t]lte_fetus_r_hair_desc=As the vernix thickens, the lanugo is shed into the amniotic fluid, and the fetus grows hair on its head.
